transcript.text: I reviewed 200 design portfolios last month.
Only 11 got a reply. Here's what they had.
One: the first screen says what you designed and what changed.
Two: every case study has one number. Not five. One.
Three: they cut the process slides nobody reads.
Comment 'review' and I'll look at yours.

onScreenText.text: 1. Outcome first  2. One number  3. Cut process

Screen recording scrolling a strong portfolio homepage
Creator crossing out process slides on an iPad

first3s.spoken: I reviewed 200 design portfolios last month.
first3s.visual: Talking head, already mid-gesture; laptop grid of 200 thumbnails behind

breakdown.headline: A big, specific sample size makes the advice feel earned before the first tip lands.

verbal.label: Proof by volume
verbal.quote: I reviewed 200 design portfolios last month.
verbal.reason: A concrete number signals authority and promises a pattern, not an opinion.

visual.label: Evidence on screen
visual.description: Laptop grid of portfolio thumbnails behind the creator from frame one.
visual.reason: Viewers can see the 200 portfolios, so the claim feels real.

onScreen.label: Outcome gap
onScreen.reason: The tiny success rate creates a gap the viewer wants closed.

hook.summary: Number + visible proof + a surprising ratio, all inside 3 seconds.

whyItWorked.detail: The 200-portfolio sample makes the tips feel like data, not opinion.
Each tip is short enough to test against your own portfolio immediately.
A one-word comment invites replies and lifts reach.

borrow: Open with the size of what you looked at (reviews, calls, projects) and the surprising result.
Keep the payoff to three rules a viewer can check in 10 seconds.
End with a one-word comment CTA tied to a real offer.
breakdown.hookTemplate: I [reviewed/ran/tested] [big number] [things] last [period]. Only [small number] [got result]. Here's what they had.

content.title: What 30 fintech onboarding flows taught me

hooks.text: I went through 30 fintech onboarding flows. Only 4 didn't make me quit.
Most fintech apps lose you before you see the home screen.
hooks.why: Bold claim tied to a pain

hooks.text: Bhai, KYC doesn't have to feel like a government office.

lines.text: I went through 30 fintech onboarding flows. Only 4 didn't make me quit.
One: they showed the reward before asking for PAN.
Two: every step said how many were left.
Three: they let you skip what wasn't legally required.
Comment 'flow' and I'll share the full breakdown.

content.cta: Comment 'flow' and I'll share the full breakdown.
content.caption: 30 onboarding flows, 4 that worked. Saving you the KYC pain.
